analysis: The trial executed successfully but the objective change reduced host validation macro HR@10 to 0.4437, compared with the reported prior HistoryModel result of 0.4775 and SASRec baseline of 0.505. Current category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.530, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.460, Electronics 0.305, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.480. Electronics remained at the reported prior 0.305; prior results for the other individual categories were not supplied. The hypothesized improvement from candidate competition was unsupported in this experiment. Sampled-softmax couples the positive and valid negatives through a shared denominator, changing gradient allocation relative to independent binary logistic supervision. This is a plausible mechanism for the regression, not an established explanation. The reported architecture, sampling, and optimization were preserved, making this evidence against this particular objective replacement within HistoryModel; it does not establish that sampled-softmax generally underperforms. No held-out test conclusions are available.
code_summary: One independent HistoryModel is trained from scratch per category and prediction loads exactly one selected checkpoint for each route. The network uses tied 128-dimensional input/output item embeddings, learned positions, two four-head causal Transformer blocks, and last-state, mean, and two learned recency-biased attention pools. An MLP with a mean residual and LayerNorm produces a normalized context. Scores use its dot product with item embeddings, a clamped learned scale, and jointly trained item biases. The sole experimental change replaces binary logistic loss with mean sampled-softmax cross-entropy over one positive and 64 uniform negative draws; target/history collisions are masked and duplicate negatives retained. Prefix sampling, AdamW, learning-rate reductions, gradient clipping, validation scheduling, early stopping, and single-best-checkpoint selection remain unchanged. The generated predictor imports the trained architecture and preserves category routing. No ensembles or separately fitted scoring components are used.
